questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code manages the logging context (MDC) across requests and threads? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.

Booking logs use `log.info("appointment booked", kv("appointmentId", id), ...)` instead of `log.info("appointment " + id + " booked")`. With the LogstashEncoder configured, what is the practical difference?
choices: There is no difference; both produce the same JSON line
The message text stays constant and each value becomes its own JSON field, so lines can be grouped by message and filtered by appointmentId
The key-value form is faster because SLF4J skips formatting entirely
The key-value form is written to a separate file for structured data

questions.prompt: At 17:00 `DayBeforeReminderJob.run` calls `reminders.sendDayBefore` for each appointment. On a `reminder-` pool thread, what MDC entries do the "reminder sent" log lines carry?
choices: None, because worker threads never inherit MDC from other threads
The requestId of whichever HTTP request last used that pool thread
The jobRunId set by the job, because the TaskDecorator copies the submitting thread's MDC when the task is submitted
Only the clinicId of the first appointment in the batch

questions.prompt: A developer adds `MDC.put("patientName", name)` in the booking flow to help debugging. Given the logback configuration, what appears in the JSON logs?
choices: patientName is added to every line written while it is set
The application fails to start because unknown MDC keys are rejected
patientName appears only on lines logged at ERROR level
patientName is omitted, because only the whitelisted MDC keys requestId, clinicId and jobRunId are included
